name: Qwen3 VL 8B Thinking
description:
Here is how to read the Qwen3 VL 8B Thinking config.json. The architecture class is Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 4,096: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 151,936 × 4,096: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 32, so each head sees 128 dimensions (4,096 / 32). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 4096 / 32 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 8, so this is grouped-query attention (GQA): 32 query heads share 8 key/value groups, so the KV cache is about 4× smaller than full MHA.

num_hidden_layers is 36: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 12,288. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 4,096-wide stream is projected up, activated with silu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 262,144 tokens — the context window in the config. rope_scaling is present ({"mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [24, 20, 20], "rope_type": "default"}). rope_theta is 5000000: that is the wavelength of the rotary embedding. A larger theta keeps distant tokens from aliasing after a full rotation.

vocab_size is 151,936. 151,936 is divisible by 128. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is false, so the input embedding matrix and the output LM head are separate learned matrices rather than a shared transpose.

torch_dtype is bfloat16. Brain floating point keeps FP32’s exponent range with less mantissa, which avoids the overflow/underflow of a tiny exponent at the cost of noisier decimals — and it halves the on-chip footprint versus FP32. NVIDIA A100s were the first NVIDIA chips with native BF16; Huawei Ascend 910-class parts also prefer BF16/FP16 on the cube.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking/blob/main/config.json.
